description: INNER, JOIN, LEFT and CROSS are live-legal unquoted column names everywhere a name goes - definitions, bare and qualified references, WHERE, GROUP BY, ORDER BY, aggregate arguments, UPDATE SET targets - while CASE works in a definition and after a dot but a BARE leading case is live's syntax error; a table may be NAMED inner but not read bare in FROM (the join grammar owns that spot); and join parsing itself is untouched. All live-measured. Converted 1:1 from ddl/KeywordColumnNamesTest (now retired). Plus the missing-relation naming matrix: bare names stay bare for SELECT/UPDATE/DELETE (Object) and INSERT (Table), TRUNCATE and DROP expand a bare name fully, partial qualification always expands, and missing schema/database sentences (schema carries its database, database stands alone). Converted 1:1 from ddl/MissingRelationNamingTest (now retired).
